author: sjm41
body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**
ARBA00022759
ARBA00022722

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel translin (FBgn0033528) (Q7JVK6)
  
* **Description of issue**
[ARBA: ARBA00022759](https://www.uniprot.org/arba/ARBA00022759) -> [#Endonuclease](https://www.uniprot.org/keywords/KW-0255) (KW-0255) -> [endonuclease activity (GO:0004519)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0004519)
[ARBA: ARBA00022722](https://www.uniprot.org/arba/ARBA00022722) -> Nuclease (KW-0540) -> [nuclease activity (GO:0004518)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0004518)

Looks like these ARBA rules are applied because of a FunFam match in translin.

Although translin forms the Trsn/Trax, ribonuclease complex, it's the Trax (not translin) component that is a catalytic subunit.
title: ARBA2GO issue: ARBA00022759 & ARBA00022722

author: sjm41
body:
Dmel CG32095 (FBgn0052095, Q95U65) and Dmel CG43088 (FBgn0262534, M9NGE9) also get KW nuclease via [ARBA: ARBA00022722](https://www.uniprot.org/arba/ARBA00022722).

In these cases, it's because of this combination of matches:
InterPro signature [IPR027806](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/IPR027806) Harbinger transposase-derived nuclease domain
InterPro signature [IPR045249](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/IPR045249) Putative nuclease HARBI1-like

Though neither of those entries have any associated GO annotations, and the entries say:
IPR027806 "This domain is found in proteins that are related to IPR001584 and are probably endonucleases of the DDE superfamily. Proteins containing this domain include the putative nuclease HARBI1. HARBI1 is a transposase-derived protein that may have nuclease activity potential"
IPR045249 "Proteins in this family may have nuclease activity"

So not very convincing.

author: Antonialock
body: Thanks Steven, It looks like the curator that updated these entries got translin and trax mixed up. I'm updating the entries to correct this.

author: Antonialock
body: actually there is a 2004 mouse paper (15491149) that says that translin has RNase activity. There are some strange conditions in the experiments, which the authors attempt to explain, but since later papers dont corroborate this I'm removing the annotations.
